name: Franklin County, IA
findings: Franklin County has 55 nonprofit organizations. 10 of them (18%) list at least one way to get involved in their tax returns or on their websites: membership, volunteering, public events, or civic and political action.
The most common is membership, listed by 8 organizations.
Social and fraternal organizations are the largest group offering opportunities (33% of those with an identified type).
Compared with 10 similar places, Franklin County has fewer organizations offering opportunities per resident.

observations.title: Fewer organizations list membership
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Franklin County list membership in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 62% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 13 organizations here; 33% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: Does that match what people here experience? Where do people find groups to join now, including outside formal organizations?

observations.title: Social and fraternal organizations that list no opportunities
observations.text: 7 social and fraternal organizations here list none of the four kinds of opportunity in their tax returns or on their websites. Many may still offer them without describing them there.

confidence.text: Based on 7 organizations here; 33% of all organizations here have no identified type.

observations.question: What do social and fraternal organizations here do in the community? How do people find out about them?

observations.title: Fewer organizations list public events
observations.text: Per resident, fewer organizations in Franklin County list public events in their tax returns or on their websites than in 10 similar places (about 70% of the typical level).

confidence.text: Based on 11 organizations here; 33% of all organizations here have no identified type.
